commentary: Today, DCE iron ore conƟnued to hold up well, with the most-traded contract I2601 closing at 791.5 yuan, up 0.76% from the previous trading day. Traders sold at market prices, while steel mills showed limited inquiries and procured at lower prices. Overall market senƟment was moderate. In Shandong, PB ﬁnes traded at 785-795 yuan, basically ﬂat from yesterday’s transacƟon price; in Hebei, 60.8% PB ﬁnes dominated transacƟons at 795-800 yuan/mt, also basically ﬂat from the previous day. According to the SMM survey, as of November 19, the blast furnace operaƟng rate across 242 steel mills tracked by SMM stood at 86.60%, up 0.04 percentage point MoM. Daily average hot metal producƟon at the sampled mills was 2.3957 million mt, down 2,000 mt WoW. Recently, maintenance plans for blast furnaces have been delayed, resulƟng in a relaƟvely small decline in hot metal output. Iron ore demand conƟnues to provide strong support for ore prices. However, considering that iron ore supply is sƟll growing and inventory pressure is gradually increasing, upward room in the short term is limited, and prices may maintain a ﬂuctuaƟng trend within a narrow range.
